deviations.what: initial noise from np.random.default_rng(seed) (video, then audio latents) instead of diffusers' torch.Generator
deviations.why: AGENTS.md determinism rule: parity runs pass the same arrays to both implementations. A given seed therefore does not reproduce a diffusers or ComfyUI run with the same seed.

deviations.what: cached text embeddings with a padding mask are trimmed to the valid tokens before the DiT
deviations.why: diffusers' __call__ takes prompt_embeds without a mask, so a run from cached embeddings must drop the padding (the study notebook does the same); report 05 shows trimming leaves the model output unchanged (rel_max 1.5e-6 in float32).

deviations.what: guidance_scale > 1 raises NotImplementedError; batch size 1 only; output is float frames in [0, 1] (output_type='np') plus the waveform, no PIL
deviations.why: distilled checkpoints use guidance 1 (CFG is spec 13); the MVP needs one video

deviations.what: release_transformer frees the DiT after denoising (scripts/generate.py sets it)
deviations.why: the spec's run order (free the DiT before decoding); keeping it adds about 7 GB to both decode peaks

deviations.what: for the bf16 run the absolute thresholds (per-step cosine >= 0.999, frames PSNR >= 30 dB) are replaced by relative ones: rel_l2 <= 2 x torch bf16 drift at every step and frames PSNR within 1 dB of torch bf16
deviations.why: the reference itself misses the absolute thresholds in bf16: diffusers with a bf16 DiT reaches cosine 0.9929 at step 9 and frames PSNR 27.7 dB vs its float32 run, because 10 distilled PiFlow steps amplify bf16 rounding. MLX bf16 tracks it (rel_l2 ratio <= 1.25, PSNR 27.4 dB), and the MLX float32 pipeline meets the absolute thresholds by far (cosine 1.0, PSNR 96.6 dB), so the port is exact and the bf16 gap is the model's.

deviations.what: stage B reference: denoising recorded with diffusers on this Mac (float32 on CPU, bf16 drift on MPS) from the local diffusers transformer and the converted media components; reference frames are the float32 final latents decoded by the MLX VAE
deviations.why: the torch CPU VAE decode needs about 25 GB and pushed the Mac into 9.4 GB of swap (the memory guard stopped it); the MLX VAE matches the torch VAE on real weights at PSNR 121.7 dB (report 08), far below this comparison's differences. Audio was decoded by torch.

architecture_notes.note: Denoising 10 steps takes 13.3 s (1.33 s/step; the study repository's Kaggle 2xT4 run took about 13 s), the video decode 7.6 s warm and 14-24 s cold, the audio decode 0.35 s. The VAE is half of a Smoke generation when cold.
architecture_notes.optimization: VAE first: sub-pixel upsample convs and fused GroupNorm (report 08), and avoiding the cold start below.

architecture_notes.note: The first decode in a process takes 16.4 s vs 7.6 s for the next ones: reading 1 GB of weights from disk, compiling Metal kernels for new shapes and getting about 20 GB of fresh memory from the OS. Clearing MLX's cache after the DiT returns its 8 GB to the OS, so the VAE cannot reuse those buffers.
architecture_notes.optimization: Keep the cache when the next stage is larger, prefetch VAE weights during the last denoising step, or decode tiles small enough that buffers are reused (spec 10/14).

architecture_notes.note: Peaks with the DiT released: denoise 8.1 GiB, video decode 20.3 GiB, audio decode 4.6 GiB; with the DiT kept, 27.2 and 11.5 GiB. The VAE decode is now the pipeline's peak.
architecture_notes.optimization: For the 16 GB profile (spec 14) the VAE must drop below about 10 GB: spatial tiles and a smaller conv chunk budget.

architecture_notes.note: Two PiFlow schedulers (video, audio) and the latent concatenation per step are negligible next to the 1.3 s DiT call.

architecture_notes.topic: bf16 vs float32 for the whole pipeline
architecture_notes.note: Over 10 PiFlow steps the bf16 DiT drifts to latent rel_l2 0.12 (cosine 0.993) and frames PSNR 27 dB vs float32, in diffusers as in MLX; per-step drift grows about 1.6x per step from step 3. The MLX float32 pipeline is exact (PSNR 96.6 dB) and at Smoke nearly as fast: denoise 14.5 s vs 13.4 s, peak 13.2 vs 8.1 GiB.
architecture_notes.optimization: Offer float32 as the quality setting for Smoke-size runs on 32 GB+ Macs; for bf16, keep the drift-sensitive parts (block 14, report 05; the last steps) in float32 and measure (spec 14).

architecture_notes.topic: batch generation keeps the DiT resident
architecture_notes.note: scripts/generate_presets.py keeps the pipeline for several videos, so the VAE decode peaks at 27-28 GiB (DiT + VAE) instead of 20.3 GiB; four Smoke videos took 22-24 s each after a one-time 1 s text encode.
architecture_notes.optimization: For 16 GB profiles release and reload the DiT per video, or decode all videos after all denoising runs.

architecture_notes.note: np.array() of a transposed MLX array is not C-contiguous, and safetensors.numpy.save_file writes the raw buffer, silently scrambling it (this produced a wrong 8.8 dB frames reference until caught). PyAV's VideoFrame.from_ndarray handles strides correctly; kandinsky6_mlx.utils.fixtures.save_fixture already copies to contiguous.
architecture_notes.optimization: Always np.ascontiguousarray before safetensors.numpy (done in scripts/encode_prompt.py).
